rubric.evidence: Every exposure and behavior claim traces to a primary source fetched 2026-08-09: the [Exposed(Window StableBlinkFeatures, DedicatedWorker LongAnimationFrameWorker)] annotations and the [RuntimeEnabled=LongAnimationFrameWorker] scriptCount attribute are quoted verbatim from the Blink IDL (trunk, verified identical on branch-heads/7978); the 200ms kCongestionThreshold, single-task trigger, and blockingDuration = duration - 200ms come from the M153-branch animation_frame_timing_monitor.cc read in full at the worker path; zeroed renderStart/styleAndLayoutStart/firstUIEventTimestamp derive from worker_performance.cc (no timestamps set) plus performance.cc (null -> 0.0); absent paintTime/presentationTime and window/windowAttribution from the [Exposed=Window] scoping in paint_timing_mixin.idl and performance_script_timing.idl. The M153-vs-trunk behavioral divergence is disclosed instead of papered over.

Folder v153/ matches the milestone=153 listing where the feature id 5387465121726464 appears under 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' (verified 2026-08-09); the dev-trial stage in the API record carries desktop_first=153. Slug derived from the exact listing name 'Support Long Animation Frames API in Web Workers' via the repo slugify rules; H1 is the listing name.

reference-contract.json declares 4 inventory items (worker exposure, scriptCount attribute with its own child route, worker entry field semantics, reporting algorithm) x 9 dimensions, each documented or not-applicable with a sourced rationale. Deliberately marked 'partial' overall: the reporting model has already changed between the M153 branch and trunk, and no normative spec text exists, so the contract cannot honestly be pinned as implementation-sufficient yet.

The page documents the DELTA against the MDN-covered base API rather than duplicating it: the lede links MDN for the base, the attribute tables answer 'which members are populated, zeroed, or absent in a worker' one by one, and the M153-vs-trunk section separates what the dev trial ships from where the design is going. Explainer features that are NOT implemented (cadence, executionContext, durationThreshold, OffscreenCanvas cadence, main-thread congested moments) are called out explicitly to prevent readers coding against them.

Overview has a complete worker-side feature-detect + observe + per-script-attribution snippet patterned on the M153 WPT; the child page has a scriptCount classification example distinguishing flood vs long-task shapes. All code in semantic <pre><code> with < and & escaped. No CPS iframe: the showcase route 404s (verified 2026-08-09), stated honestly with the WICG live demo (verified 200) as the runnable alternative.

BCD checked for the worker delta specifically: no worker_support subfeature on PerformanceLongAnimationFrameTiming or PerformanceScriptTiming and no scriptCount member (full BCD dataset walked 2026-08-09), so the compat tables are labelled interim and split 'base API (window)' from 'this feature (workers)' columns to avoid implying the base API's Chrome/Edge 123 support applies to workers. Baseline banner reports the base API as Baseline limited per webstatus.dev and this feature as Chrome-only behind a flag.

Every named source is a direct link: spec, open spec issue #38, explainer, intent-to-prototype Google Groups thread from the API record, tracking bug, each cited Chromium file at the exact ref (trunk or branch-heads/7978), M153-branch WPT and upstream WPT, BCD files, webstatus.dev query, and MDN pages. The docs.google.com design doc on the ChromeStatus record was deliberately not linked (access-restricted Google doc). github.com HTML URLs returned 403 through this sandbox's proxy but their content was verified via raw.githubusercontent.com and the GitHub search API; the canonical URLs are used.

Single h1, sequential h2 outline on both routes; all tables use th scope headers inside .table-wrap scroll containers; the Baseline banner uses role=note with aria-label; pre blocks scroll internally; colors are exclusively the shared stylesheet variables (WCAG AA per repo invariant #5); external links carry target=_blank rel=noopener.

overflow-wrap:anywhere on h1/lede/inline code for the long feature name, flag string, and file paths; tables in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with table-layout:fixed and min-width guard; verified by screenshots at 1280x2400 and 390x844 read during self-verify (no horizontal page overflow; code blocks scroll internally).

CPS feature route returns 404 (HEAD-checked 2026-08-09) so no iframe is embedded; the page links the future showcase route in see-also and offers the WICG long-task live demo (200) plus the WPT as runnable material. Should be upgraded to an embed when the showcase demo lands.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive reference documentation tables code blocks long identifiers mobile overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Lean on the browser layout engine and intrinsic sizing; keep overflow contained per container; avoid hardcoded dimensions and prefer flexible tracks/minmax over media queries.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied: doc tables render inside .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} with table-layout:fixed and overflow-wrap:anywhere on cells; route cards use grid repeat(auto-fit, minmax(16rem,1fr)); pre blocks scroll internally; no fixed pixel widths beyond min-width guards on wide tables.

guidanceConsulted.query: measuring long tasks responsiveness PerformanceObserver INP main thread
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Monitor long-animation-frame entries with PerformanceObserver, accumulate entry.scripts across callbacks, and group by sourceURL to find heavy scripts; filter noise with thresholds.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied to example accuracy: the worker example uses the same observer + scripts-attribution pattern (adapted to the worker context and the M153 200ms trigger), and the page links Chrome's LoAF guide for the accumulate-and-group technique instead of re-inventing it.

guidanceConsulted.query: measuring long tasks responsiveness PerformanceObserver INP main thread
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use field-measurable, lightweight observation APIs (LoAF/event timing) rather than heavyweight tracing for diagnosing slow interactions.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied as framing: the page positions the worker extension as field diagnostics for blocked worker event loops and cross-references the JS Self-Profiling reference for the sampling-profiler alternative.

openQuestions: The M153 branch reports a congested moment for a single task >= 200ms while trunk has moved to a queuing-delay model (backlog depth >= 2, multi-task coalescing, queue-drain finalization). Which model actually reaches users depends on when the flag flips and on future branch points - re-verify at each milestone until the feature leaves 'test' status.

forcedStyleAndLayoutDuration exists on worker PerformanceScriptTiming per the IDL; the page states no forced style/layout time is recorded in workers based on the absence of DOM style/layout on the worker path, but the probe plumbing was not traced end to end.

The explainer's cadence, executionContext, durationThreshold, and OffscreenCanvas animation-frame cadence are unimplemented as of 2026-08-09; the page must be updated the moment any of them appear in runtime_enabled_features.json5 or the IDL.
PerformanceEntry.name for worker entries is documented as 'long-animation-frame' from the shared constructor path; worth confirming in a live flagged build once one is available to this environment.

followUpGoals.goal: Re-verify LongAnimationFrameWorker's status in runtime_enabled_features.json5 at each new milestone branch; when it moves from 'test' to 'experimental' or 'stable', update the warn-block enable steps and the compatibility table, and re-derive the reporting model from that branch's animation_frame_timing_monitor.cc (single-task vs queuing-delay coalescing).

When the worker exposure gains normative text (w3c/long-animation-frames#38) or a BCD worker_support/scriptCount entry appears, replace the interim compat table with BCD-derived rows and add the spec link to Specifications; consider upgrading reference-contract.json from partial toward implementation-sufficient.
If the congested-moment cadence/executionContext properties land in Chromium, add child reference routes for them (new pages, additive) rather than expanding this overview beyond scannability.
If the Chrome Platform Showcase ships a demo route for this feature, upgrade the examples section's text fallback to the standard embedded iframe.
